title: The Great Equations: Breakthroughs in Science from Pythagoras to Heisenberg
author: Robert P. Crease
summary: A popular history of ten landmark equations, from the Pythagorean theorem and Newton's laws to Maxwell, Einstein and Heisenberg, told through the people and context behind them. Reviewers found it accessible and engaging as an introduction rather than a technical treatment.

title: The Definition of Standard ML (Revised)
author: Robin Milner, Mads Tofte, Robert Harper, David MacQueen
summary: The formal definition of Standard ML '97, giving its static and dynamic semantics as inference rules. Widely cited as a landmark: one of the few full-scale languages to be completely and rigorously specified.

title: Functional Programming for Mortals with Scalaz
author: Sam Halliday
summary: A practical guide to pure functional programming in Scala using the Scalaz library, built around a worked application and covering typeclasses, monads and effects. Well regarded in the Scala FP community for making the typelevel style approachable to working developers.

title: Domain Modeling Made Functional: Tackle Software Complexity with Domain-Driven Design and F#
author: Scott Wlaschin
summary: Combines domain-driven design with functional programming in F#, showing how algebraic types and function composition can encode business rules and make illegal states unrepresentable. Widely praised as one of the clearest arguments for type-driven domain modeling.

title: Data Scientists at Work
author: Sebastian Gutierrez
summary: A collection of interviews with sixteen practicing data scientists from industry and research about their careers, methods and the emerging profession. Valued as a snapshot of the field in its early boom years rather than as a technical text.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
summary: The long-running 'dinosaur book' covering processes, scheduling, synchronization, memory, storage and file systems. One of the most widely adopted undergraduate operating systems textbooks, in print through many editions.

title: Parallel and Concurrent Programming in Haskell
author: Simon Marlow
summary: Covers deterministic parallelism (Eval, Strategies, the Par monad, Repa, Accelerate) and concurrency with threads, MVars and STM in GHC Haskell, by a principal developer of GHC's runtime. Regarded as the definitive book on the subject.

title: The Rust Programming Language
author: Steve Klabnik and Carol Nichols
summary: The official introduction to Rust ("the book"), covering ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, traits, error handling and concurrency. The standard starting point for learning the language, maintained alongside the Rust project.

title: The Climbing Handbook: The Complete Guide to Safe and Exciting Rock Climbing
author: Steve Long
summary: An illustrated practical guide to rock climbing technique, equipment, ropework and safety by a British mountaineering instructor. A general instructional manual rather than a technical textbook.

title: Advanced Compiler Design and Implementation
author: Steven S. Muchnick
summary: An encyclopedic treatment of optimizing compilers: intermediate representations, data-flow and alias analysis, register allocation, scheduling and loop optimizations. Long a standard professional reference for back-end optimization.

title: The Algorithm Design Manual
author: Steven S. Skiena
summary: A practical algorithms text pairing design techniques and 'war stories' with a large catalog of standard problems and their known solutions. Popular with practitioners and for interview preparation for its applied, problem-oriented approach.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
summary: The comprehensive algorithms textbook known as CLRS, covering sorting, data structures, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, NP-completeness and more with rigorous analysis. The most widely used algorithms text in universities worldwide.

title: Coordinated MultiPoint Transmission with Incomplete Information
author: Tilak Rajesh Lakshmana
summary: A Chalmers University of Technology doctoral thesis on coordinated multipoint (CoMP) transmission in cellular networks when channel and data information at base stations is incomplete. An academic research work with no wider critical reception.

title: Efficient Backhauling in Cooperative MultiPoint Cellular Networks
author: Tilak Rajesh Lakshmana
summary: A Chalmers University of Technology thesis studying how to reduce backhaul load in cooperative multipoint cellular systems. An academic research work, a precursor to the author's later doctoral thesis.

title: F# Deep Dives
author: Tomas Petricek, Phillip Trelford (eds.)
summary: A collection of chapters by F# practitioners applying the language to real domains such as finance, data science, games and web development. Valued as a showcase of applied functional programming rather than a language tutorial.

title: Proof of Stake: The Making of Ethereum and the Philosophy of Blockchains
author: Vitalik Buterin (ed. Nathan Schneider)
summary: A curated collection of Buterin's essays from 2014 to 2021 on Ethereum's design, proof-of-stake consensus, governance and public goods. Reviewers saw it as a useful record of the thinking behind Ethereum, though uneven as a book.

title: Wing Chun Bil Jee: The Deadly Art of Thrusting Fingers
author: William Cheung
summary: An Ohara Publications manual on Bil Jee, the third empty-hand form of Wing Chun kung fu, by a senior student of Ip Man. A martial arts instructional book, not a technical text.

title: Harmonica for Dummies
author: Winslow Yerxa
summary: A beginner's guide to the diatonic harmonica covering breathing, single notes, bending and playing blues, folk and rock styles. Well reviewed by learners as a thorough introduction for a self-help music book.

title: The Japanese Abacus Explained
author: Yozo Yoshino
summary: A classic guide to soroban arithmetic, explaining addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and roots on the Japanese abacus, reprinted by Dover. Valued as a clear, complete older manual on abacus technique.

title: System Design Interview: An Insider's Guide, Vol. 1
author: Alex Xu
summary: Walks through common system design interview problems such as rate limiters, URL shorteners, news feeds and chat systems with a repeatable framework and diagrams. One of the most popular system design interview prep books, though critics note it stays at a high level.

title: C++ Primer
author: Stanley B. Lippman & Josée Lajoie
summary: A thorough introduction to C++ updated for the then-new ISO C++98 standard, covering the language, the standard library and templates. A long-standing standard tutorial reference for the language.

title: Data Structures, Algorithms, and Applications in C++
author: Sartaj Sahni
summary: An undergraduate data structures text implementing lists, trees, graphs, hashing and sorting in C++, with many applications and exercises. Widely used in university courses, particularly in India.

title: Computer Networks
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum
summary: A layered survey of networking from the physical layer through protocols such as TCP/IP to applications and security. One of the classic networking textbooks, known for its readable style.

title: Fundamentals of Database Systems
author: Ramez Elmasri & Shamkant B. Navathe
summary: A comprehensive database text covering ER modeling, the relational model, SQL, normalization, storage, indexing and transactions. One of the most widely adopted database textbooks.

title: Mathematical Statistics with Applications
author: Dennis D. Wackerly, William Mendenhall, Richard L. Scheaffer
summary: A calculus-based introduction to probability and statistical inference covering distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing and regression. A standard upper-undergraduate mathematical statistics text.

title: Database Management Systems
author: Raghu Ramakrishnan & Johannes Gehrke
summary: Covers relational databases from query languages and design through storage, indexing, query evaluation and optimization, and transactions (the 'cow book'). Respected for its strong treatment of DBMS internals.

title: Intro Stats
author: Richard De Veaux, Paul Velleman, David Bock
summary: An introductory, data-first statistics textbook emphasizing reasoning, graphics and real examples over formulas. Popular for introductory and AP statistics courses for its conversational style.

title: Engineering Mathematics (VTU)
author: D. S. Chandrasekharaiah
summary: A Bangalore-published engineering mathematics textbook written to the Visvesvaraya Technological University syllabus, covering calculus, differential equations, transforms and related applied topics. A regional course text with little published review.

title: Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice
author: William Stallings
summary: Covers symmetric and public-key cryptography, hashing, authentication and network security protocols. A standard undergraduate security textbook through many editions.

title: Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment
author: W. Richard Stevens
summary: A detailed guide to the UNIX system-call interface: files, processes, signals, terminals, IPC and daemons. Regarded as the classic reference for UNIX systems programming.

title: Discrete Mathematical Structures
author: Bernard Kolman, Robert C. Busby, Sharon Ross
summary: An introductory discrete mathematics text for computer science students covering logic, sets, relations, graphs, trees, Boolean algebra and automata. A commonly used course textbook.

title: Scala for the Impatient
author: Cay S. Horstmann
summary: A fast-paced, example-driven introduction to Scala for experienced programmers, updated in this edition for Scala 3. Well regarded as a concise practical guide.

title: AI Engineering: Building Applications with Foundation Models
author: Chip Huyen
summary: Covers building products on foundation models: evaluation, prompt engineering, RAG, agents, finetuning, dataset engineering and inference optimization. Widely praised and a bestseller as a practical overview of the LLM application stack.

title: The Hundred-Page Language Models Book
author: Andriy Burkov
summary: A compact introduction to language models, building from ML basics and count-based models through RNNs to Transformers and LLM practice, with code. Follows the well-received format of the author's Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book. (Title inferred from a partly hidden spine.)

title: Introductory Probability and Statistical Applications
author: Paul L. Meyer
summary: A classic engineering-oriented probability and statistics text covering random variables, distributions, reliability and inference. Long used in engineering curricula, especially in India.

title: Distributed Computing Through Combinatorial Topology
author: Maurice Herlihy, Dmitry Kozlov, Sergio Rajsbaum
summary: Develops the topological approach to distributed computability, modeling protocols as simplicial complexes to prove possibility and impossibility results. The standard reference for this research area.

title: The Little Book of Semaphores
author: Allen B. Downey
summary: A free textbook teaching synchronization through a sequence of classical and novel concurrency puzzles solved with semaphores. Popular as a hands-on supplement to operating systems courses.

title: Zionomicon
author: John A. De Goes & Adam Fraser
summary: A comprehensive guide to ZIO, the Scala library for typed functional effects, covering fibers, error handling, resources, STM, streams and testing, by ZIO's creator and a core contributor. The main book-length reference for ZIO.

title: The Dravidian Languages
author: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti
summary: A comprehensive comparative and historical study of the Dravidian language family, covering phonology, morphology, syntax and reconstruction of Proto-Dravidian. Regarded as the definitive modern survey of the family.

title: The Science of Functional Programming: A Tutorial, with Examples in Scala
author: Sergei Winitzki
summary: A long, free textbook deriving functional programming techniques (functors, monads, free structures, typeclasses) from mathematical first principles with Scala examples. Noted for its rigor and proofs, more mathematical than most FP books.

title: Linear Algebra via Exterior Products
author: Sergei Winitzki
summary: A free text presenting finite-dimensional linear algebra in a coordinate-free way through exterior products, deriving determinants and related results without matrices. Known as an unusual and elegant alternative approach.

title: Div, Grad, Curl, and All That: An Informal Text on Vector Calculus
author: H. M. Schey
summary: An informal introduction to vector calculus motivated through electrostatics, building divergence, gradient, curl and the integral theorems intuitively. A beloved supplement for physics and engineering students.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
author: Richard S. Sutton & Andrew G. Barto
summary: The foundational reinforcement learning textbook covering bandits, MDPs, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo and temporal-difference methods, function approximation and policy gradients. The standard reference for the field, by two of its founders.

title: A Generative Grammar of Kannada
author: A. K. Ramanujan
summary: A. K. Ramanujan's Indiana University doctoral dissertation applying early transformational-generative grammar to Kannada. Of mainly historical and specialist interest; little published criticism exists.

title: An Introduction to Functional Programming Through Lambda Calculus
author: Greg Michaelson
summary: Builds functional programming from the untyped lambda calculus up through data structures, recursion and evaluation strategies, with links to Lisp and ML. Valued as a gentle, self-contained introduction (reprinted by Dover).

title: Pragmatic Type-Level Design
author: Alexander Granin
summary: Explores practical type-level programming in Haskell for application design, including type-level DSLs and extensible architectures. A niche, self-published work aimed at experienced Haskell developers.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
author: Kenneth H. Rosen
summary: A comprehensive discrete mathematics text covering logic, proofs, sets, number theory, counting, graphs and automata with many exercises. One of the most widely used discrete math textbooks for computer science.

title: Advanced Topics in Types and Programming Languages
author: Benjamin C. Pierce (ed.)
summary: An edited sequel to TAPL with chapters on substructural types, dependent types, effect systems, module systems, type inference and typed assembly language. A standard graduate-level reference.

title: Algebra, Topology, Differential Calculus, and Optimization Theory for Computer Science and Machine Learning
author: Jean Gallier & Jocelyn Quaintance
summary: A very large free text from the University of Pennsylvania covering the mathematics underlying ML, from topology and differential calculus to convex optimization, SVMs and kernel methods. Known for its breadth and rigor.

title: Linear Algebra for Computer Vision, Robotics, and Machine Learning
author: Jean Gallier & Jocelyn Quaintance
summary: A rigorous, extensive free treatment of linear algebra and matrix decompositions (SVD, QR, spectral theory) with applications to vision, robotics and ML. A companion to the authors' optimization volume.

title: The Implementation of Functional Programming Languages
author: Simon L. Peyton Jones
summary: Explains how lazy functional languages are compiled: translation to lambda calculus, pattern matching, type checking and graph reduction including the G-machine. A classic foundation for later work such as GHC.

title: Implementing Functional Languages: A Tutorial
author: Simon L. Peyton Jones & David R. Lester
summary: A hands-on guide to building implementations of a small lazy language, progressing through template instantiation, the G-machine, TIM and a parallel G-machine. Widely used as a practical companion to the 1987 book.

title: Functional Programming in Lean
author: David Thrane Christiansen
summary: The official free introduction to Lean 4 as a programming language, covering structures, typeclasses, monads, dependent types and programs with proofs. The recommended starting point for programming in Lean.

title: Unix System Programming in OCaml
author: Xavier Leroy & Didier Rémy
summary: A course on UNIX systems programming (files, processes, signals, pipes, sockets, threads) using OCaml's Unix library, by two of OCaml's designers. A respected free text for systems programming in a functional language.

title: The Formal Semantics of Programming Languages: An Introduction
author: Glynn Winskel
summary: Introduces operational, denotational and axiomatic semantics, domain theory and recursive types, with careful proofs. A standard graduate textbook on semantics.

title: Conceptual Mathematics: A First Introduction to Categories
author: F. William Lawvere & Stephen H. Schanuel
summary: An elementary, discussion-driven introduction to category theory assuming little background, by one of the field's founders. Praised for its gentle approach, though some readers find its pace slow.

title: Universal Algebra
author: P. M. Cohn
summary: A classic monograph on the general theory of algebraic structures: varieties, free algebras, lattices and model-theoretic aspects. One of the standard early texts of the field.

title: Graph Theory and Additive Combinatorics: Exploring Structure and Randomness
author: Yufei Zhao
summary: A graduate text from Zhao's MIT course covering Szemerédi's regularity lemma, pseudorandomness, graph limits, and the links between graph theory and additive combinatorics such as Roth's theorem. Well received as a modern, unified treatment.

title: Basic Category Theory for Computer Scientists
author: Benjamin C. Pierce
summary: A short introduction to categories, functors, natural transformations, adjunctions and cartesian closed categories with applications to computing. A popular concise first text for programmers.

title: Introducing Category Theory
author: Peter Smith
summary: A freely available, carefully paced introduction to category theory by a Cambridge logician, aimed at self-learners with some mathematical background. Valued for its clarity and leisurely explanations.

title: Type Theory and Functional Programming
author: Simon Thompson
summary: An introduction to Martin-Löf constructive type theory as a foundation for functional programming and program verification. A well-known text, now freely available online.

title: Introduction to Logic and to the Methodology of the Deductive Sciences
author: Alfred Tarski
summary: Tarski's introductory text on sentential logic, quantifiers, identity, classes and relations, and the axiomatic method, illustrated with arithmetic. A classic of logic pedagogy translated into many languages.

title: Practical Foundations for Programming Languages
author: Robert Harper
summary: A unified type-theoretic account of programming language concepts (statics, dynamics, polymorphism, effects, concurrency, modules) using structural operational semantics. A demanding standard graduate text.

title: Intuitionistic Type Theory
author: Per Martin-Löf
summary: Notes from Martin-Löf's 1980 Padua lectures presenting his constructive type theory, the basis of proof assistants such as Agda and NuPRL. A foundational primary source of the field.

title: Lambda-Calculus and Combinators: An Introduction
author: J. Roger Hindley & Jonathan P. Seldin
summary: A rigorous introduction to untyped and typed lambda calculus and combinatory logic, covering reduction, computability and type assignment. A standard introductory text.

title: An Infinite Descent into Pure Mathematics
author: Clive Newstead
summary: A free introduction to proofs and pure mathematics developed for Carnegie Mellon's transition course, covering logic, sets, number theory, combinatorics and real numbers. Well regarded for clarity.

title: Theorem Proving in Lean 4
author: Jeremy Avigad, Leonardo de Moura, Soonho Kong, Sebastian Ullrich
summary: The official tutorial on using Lean 4 as a proof assistant, covering dependent type theory, propositions as types, tactics, inductive types and type classes. The standard introduction to formal proof in Lean.

title: Intuitive Topology
author: V. V. Prasolov
summary: A short, picture-driven introduction to topological ideas such as knots, surfaces, vector fields and the Euler characteristic, aimed at students with little background. Published in the AMS Mathematical World series.

title: Algebraic Topology: An Intuitive Approach
author: Hajime Sato
summary: A concise introduction to homotopy, homology, fiber bundles and related ideas emphasizing intuition over full rigor, translated from Japanese for the AMS. Useful as a gentle overview before more formal texts.

title: Effect Oriented Programming
author: Bill Frasure, Bruce Eckel, James Ward
summary: Introduces managing side effects, errors and dependencies as typed effects, with examples in Scala 3 and ZIO. Aimed at practitioners new to effect systems.

title: Scala with Cats
author: Noel Welsh & Dave Gurnell
summary: Teaches functional abstractions such as monoids, functors, monads, applicatives and traversals through the Cats library, with case studies. A widely recommended free book for typed FP in Scala.

title: Book of Proof
author: Richard Hammack
summary: A free introduction to proof writing covering logic, sets, direct proof, contradiction, induction, relations, functions and cardinality. One of the most widely adopted open textbooks for transition-to-proof courses.

title: Module Theory: An Approach to Linear Algebra
author: T. S. Blyth
summary: Develops linear algebra through modules over rings, covering exact sequences, tensor products, the structure theorem for modules over a PID and canonical forms. A respected, rigorous text.

title: Programming Well: Abstraction and Design in Computation
author: Stuart M. Shieber
summary: The textbook for Harvard's CS51, teaching abstraction, types, functional and imperative programming, and design principles using OCaml. Aimed at second-course programming students.

title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Mathematics (But Didn't Even Know to Ask)
author: Brendan W. Sullivan
summary: Carnegie Mellon course notes introducing mathematical thinking, logic, proof techniques, sets, induction and functions for students moving to proof-based mathematics. A free, informal-in-tone text.

title: Geometric Structures on Manifolds
author: William M. Goldman
summary: A graduate monograph on locally homogeneous (G,X)-structures such as affine and projective structures, developing maps and holonomy. Published in the AMS Graduate Studies series; a standard reference for the topic.

title: Homotopy Theory
author: Sze-Tsen Hu
summary: A classic early textbook on homotopy theory covering fibre spaces, homotopy groups, obstruction theory and related topics. Historically important, though superseded by later treatments.

title: Concise Machine Learning
author: Jonathan Richard Shewchuk
summary: Lecture notes from Shewchuk's Berkeley CS 189 course covering linear classifiers, SVMs, regression, decision theory, PCA, neural networks and more. Known for clear, compact explanations.

title: Optimization for Machine Learning
author: Bernd Gärtner & Martin Jaggi
summary: ETH Zurich / EPFL lecture notes on convex and nonconvex optimization for ML, including gradient descent variants, stochastic and coordinate methods, and Newton-type methods with convergence proofs. A course text rather than a published book.

title: Compilers: Course Notes
author: Oleg Kiselyov
summary: Course notes by Oleg Kiselyov on building a compiler incrementally and extensibly, in his tagless-final style. An informal teaching resource with no published reviews.

title: Calculating Compilers
author: Erik Meijer
summary: Erik Meijer's Nijmegen doctoral dissertation on deriving compilers by program calculation in the algebraic, Bird-Meertens style. Of specialist interest; an early work in calculational program construction.

title: Surreal Numbers
author: Donald E. Knuth
summary: A short novelette in which two students discover and develop John Conway's surreal numbers from a few axioms. Celebrated as an introduction to the creative process of mathematical research.

title: The Riddle of Scheherazade: And Other Amazing Puzzles, Ancient and Modern
author: Raymond M. Smullyan
summary: A collection of logic and number puzzles framed by Scheherazade telling puzzles to the king, building toward ideas about self-reference and Gödel. In the tradition of Smullyan's well-loved puzzle books.

title: Mathematical Theory of the Transformer, Vol. I: Foundations, Rationality, and the Incremental Transformer
author: Giansalvo Cirrincione
summary: A recent Routledge monograph giving a mathematical treatment of the Transformer architecture, including the author's incremental Transformer. Too new for substantial critical reception.
